description.summary: A large-scale urban atlas style built around individual buildings, parcels, streets, materials, fire risk, occupancy, utilities, and dense abbreviations. The map should feel like a precise underwriting document: pastel color-coded buildings on cream paper, black parcel/street geometry, small technical notes, and sheet-level marginalia. Its charm comes from obsessive information density, not decorative flourish.
description.design_principle: Make buildings and fire-risk attributes the primary visual subject. Use pastel fills to encode construction materials, thin black linework to structure parcels and streets, and compact annotations to reveal occupancy, stories, roof types, hydrants, walls, tanks, elevators, and industrial hazards.
description.historical_context: fire insurance atlas Fire Insurance Maps were prepared for insurance companies and underwriters to assess fire risk in American towns and cities. Sheets typically covered only a few blocks at large scale and recorded building footprints, construction materials, number of stories, occupancy, street widths, hydrants, water mains, fire alarm boxes, industrial hazards, and other risk-relevant urban details. large-scale lithographic atlas sheets hand-applied or printed color tints bound city atlases

typography.character: Small, technical, serif-leaning or engraved-print-like typography with compact uppercase abbreviations. It should feel like lithographed urban-atlas lettering rather than a modern UI font.
typography.fallback_strategy: Prefer metrically stable, licensable fonts with the language coverage required by the map; preserve hierarchy when substitution is necessary.
rules: Use abbreviations liberally but explain them in a key or popup.
Place street names in the street corridor, not detached like web basemap labels.
Fit building-use labels inside footprints when space permits; otherwise use short callouts.
Avoid large modern label halos; use small knockout boxes only when absolutely necessary.
Use rotated labels for narrow streets and buildings when it improves fit.
Do not use playful vintage fonts; fire insurance atlas is technical, not saloon-poster ornamental.

required: Make buildings and fire-risk attributes the primary visual subject. Use pastel fills to encode construction materials, thin black linework to structure parcels and streets, and compact annotations to reveal occupancy, stories, roof types, hydrants, walls, tanks, elevators, and industrial hazards.
preferred: Make building footprints the main visual layer.
Represent streets as negative space/corridors with labels, not modern cased road symbols.
Use dense but zoom-aware annotation; reveal detail progressively.
Use popups to decode, not to replace, the visual map language.
Do not use modern Web Mercator road-tile styling as the dominant aesthetic.
Do not apply choropleth county/state fills; this is building-scale mapping.
Do not use decorative parchment, pirate-map fonts, or steampunk ornament as shortcuts for history.
Do not make color arbitrary; color must encode material or clearly declared modern categories.
Do not show too much citywide detail at once; fire insurance atlas style is block/sheet scale.
Use vector building footprints with data-driven fill colors for material/use.
Use scale-dependent rendering: index map at low zoom, block labels at medium zoom, building annotations at high zoom.
Use optional hatching or pattern overlays to support accessibility and material ambiguity.
unsupported: Exact facsimile reproduction of a named source map, protected artwork, logo, seal, interface, or trade dress.
Provider-specific behavior that has not been verified against a pinned source and style contract.

accessibility.color_independence: Because the historical system relies heavily on color, reinforce material classes with abbreviations, outline treatments, hatching, or popup text. Provide a readable legend and avoid relying on red/pink versus yellow alone for critical meaning.
accessibility.contrast: Preserve readable contrast for labels, lines, and critical symbols at intended zoom levels.
accessibility.minimum_text_size: Adapt historical or print typography to a practical screen-reading threshold.
additional: Test the compiled style in grayscale and under common color-vision simulations.
